exits.notes: First CFO tenure. 8-K: Tesla announced his 'intention to retire as Tesla's CFO'; he would 'resign as CFO ... effective as of November 30, 2015, though Deepak will remain at Tesla for the next few months'; the 2016 proxy says he 'retired from his role as Chief Financial Officer in November 2015'. His FY2015 SCT row has Bonus and All Other Compensation '—', but he stayed employed into 2016 (end day not disclosed; he was not an NEO for FY2016), so no filing quantifies any pay tied to his eventual departure; all components null. Tesla discloses no severance or termination arrangements for NEOs ("we do not have any contract, agreement, plan or arrangement that would result in payments to a named executive officer at, following, or in connection with any termination"). Basis 'estimated' because only that no-arrangement statement covers the departure. He rejoined as CFO on 2017-03-02.

Nothing quantified; all components null. Tesla discloses no severance or termination arrangements for NEOs ("we do not have any contract, agreement, plan or arrangement that would result in payments to a named executive officer at, following, or in connection with any termination").

conflicts.description: Mizuno's 2021-2022 fees vs. later 'no compensation for 2021 and 2022'. The FY2021 tables (2022 10-K/A and DEF 14A) print Mizuno fees of 27,500 plus 10,949 travel reimbursement, and the FY2022 table (2023 DEF 14A) prints fees of 27,500. Mizuno is one of the eleven Director Defendants. The July 2023 settlement says Director Defendants 'shall not hereafter receive any compensation for Tesla Board service for 2021 or 2022' (forward-looking), and the 2025 10-K/A says the Board 'will not receive' it, but the 2025 DEF 14A says 'the Board did not receive any compensation for Board service for 2021 and 2022'. No later table restates the FY2021 or FY2022 rows, and no filing says whether Mizuno's fees were repaid. Rows are recorded as printed.

The FY2018-FY2020 director option awards are recorded as printed (grant-date fair values). The Detroit derivative suit (filed 2020-06-17) challenged non-employee director awards from 2017 through 2020. Under the July 2023 settlement (approved 2025-01-08, final judgment 2025-01-13, affirmed by the Delaware Supreme Court 2026-01-30), the eleven Director Defendants returned value of $735,266,505: $458,649,785 in returned options (1,957,861 unexercised options, cancelled May 2025) and $276,616,720 in cash and/or stock (Tesla 'received $277 million from certain directors' in Q1 2025). No later Director Compensation Table restates the earlier years. Per-director amounts appear only for Denholm (about $6,196,458 of grant-date fair value forfeited, about 40% of her 2018-2020 awards) and Wilson-Thompson (about $2,610,474, about 36% of her 2019 awards), in the 2025 proxy's Special Committee report. These are not restatements, so no row amounts were changed.

Three-cell rows in four-column tables. In FY2019 (2020 10-K/A, DEF 14A, DEFA14A) and FY2020 (2021 10-K/A, DEF 14A), Kimbal Musk's row prints '20,000 — 20,000', and in FY2020 Mizuno's row prints '18,963 9,209,853 9,228,816'. Kimbal's missing cell is a zero either way. Mizuno's middle figure is recorded as Option Awards (it equals total minus fees, and the table footnote lists 117,230 options outstanding for him) with All Other at 0.

Ahuja's 2015 exit is described as a resignation in the 8-K ('Deepak will resign as CFO ... effective as of November 30, 2015') and a retirement in the 2016 proxy ('retired from his role as Chief Financial Officer in November 2015'); the 8-K also refers to his 'intention to retire'. Recorded as 'retired'.

open_questions: Per-director split of the Detroit settlement: the filings give the aggregate ($735,266,505 = $458,649,785 returned options + $276,616,720 cash/stock; 1,957,861 options cancelled; $277 million cash received) and approximate forfeitures for Denholm and Wilson-Thompson only. How much each of the other nine Director Defendants returned, in cash, stock or options, is not in any Tesla filing reviewed (the Stipulation itself, filed with the Court of Chancery, is not an SEC exhibit).
Whether Mizuno's FY2021-FY2022 cash fees (27,500 each year) were repaid or are covered by the settlement's 'shall not hereafter receive' wording is not stated (see conflicts).

Future director pay: as of the 2026-04-30 10-K/A all eight outside directors waive cash and the Board continues to forgo option grants until it 'acts to amend the Director Compensation Policy'. The settlement requires any non-employee director compensation to be approved annually by unaffiliated stockholders. No 2026 DEF 14A has been filed through 2026-10-08, so FY2026 policy is unknown.

Exit pay that falls after the departure year is not covered by any SCT: Ahuja's advisory role after March 2019 (fees and end date not disclosed) and his 2015-2016 transition employment (he stayed 'for the next few months' after 2015-11-30). Straubel (July 2019) and Guillen's August 2015 role end have no departure-year SCT row and no 8-K.
Unvested equity forfeited on departure (Guillen 2021, Kirkhorn 2023, Baglino 2024) is described but never quantified, so accelerated_equity_value is null rather than 0 for every exit.
